ex: This test is easy.
Is the hotel easy to find?
Is English easy for you?
This game is too easy for me.
easy.say: easy to find · easy for me · too easy
easy.why: examples B1: past tense, 8-10 words, one question; no Say line

ex: Wash your face and hands.
Is there something on my face?
Your face is red. Are you OK?
She has a kind face.
face.why: past tense, future 'will', 8-9 words; only one question

ex: Are you in trouble?
I have trouble with my phone.
Sorry for the trouble.
Call me if you have any trouble.
trouble.say: be in trouble · have trouble with
trouble.why: past tense, 8-9 words, one question; no Say line

ex: Give me a chance.
Is there a chance of rain today?
Do I have a chance?
I want another chance.
chance.why: calques: 'This is a good chance.', 'Do you have a chance to call?'

ex: I watch videos on my phone.
Send me the video, please.
This video is very funny.
Can you make a video?
video.why: habit needs plural: 'I watch videos', not 'a video'

ex: I live with my partner.
Find a partner and practice the dialog.
He is my business partner.
Can my partner come too?
partner.why: two sentences have 8 words (top-1000 max is 7)

ex: Do you have this model in blue?
What model is your phone?
I like this car model.
She is a fashion model.
model.why: only one question or request; top-1000 needs two

season.say: favorite season · high season · this season
season.why: 'in this season' is a calque; English says 'this season'

class.note: Often a lesson: "I have a class at nine." A school year is a "grade" (US) or "year" (UK).
class.why: add the typical error 'in fifth class' (= fifth grade)

start.why: lemma includes 'started'; the noun is only ~10% of uses

ex: Is the fight on TV today?
Can we watch the fight?
I have tickets for the fight.
The big fight is at nine.
fight.note: Most often a verb: "Don't fight!" A fight can also be a quarrel: "a fight with my brother".
fight.why: a bout/brawl is ~20% of uses; 'Anna wins the fight' unnatural; quarrel sense

file.note: Also papers about a person or a case: "The doctor has your file." Also a verb: "file a report".
file.why: only the computer file is shared; case files and the verb are common

cent.note: In British English "per cent" means % ("ten per cent"); it is not the coin.
cent.why: many uses of 'cent' are British 'per cent'

ex: My brother is gay and lives with his partner.
Are there any gay bars near here?
Many gay couples live in this part of town.
She told her parents that she is gay.
gay.why: no question or request (band needs one)

ex: My first task today is to answer emails.
Cleaning the garage is a big task.
Can you give me a new task?
She finished the task in ten minutes.
task.say: do a task · finish a task
task.why: no question or request; no Say line

ex: The new law had a big impact on business.
Social media has a huge impact on kids.
Does coffee have an impact on your sleep?
Her work made a real impact.
impact.say: have an impact on · a big impact
impact.why: no question or request; no Say line

ex: The ship is leaving the port.
We arrived at the port in the morning.
This city has a big port.
How do I get to the port?
port.why: no question or request (band needs one)

ex: The kids are going to summer camp in July.
How much does summer camp cost?
The camp has tents, a kitchen, and showers.
My son loved his first week at camp.
camp.why: no question; 'set up camp' is a phrasal idiom

ex: My sister has a strong character.
Describe your character in three words.
Sport can help to build character.
He has a calm, friendly character.
character.why: two 10-word sentences, no question, stiff wording

ex: The people at this hotel are very friendly.
She always has a friendly smile.
Is your dog friendly with small children?
Our new neighbors seem friendly and helpful.
The photo is out of focus.
How do I change the focus on this camera?
Our main focus is the customer.
What is the focus of this lesson?
focus.note: Most often a verb: "I can't focus." A magic trick is a "trick", not a "focus".
focus.say: in focus · out of focus · the main focus
focus.why: share 40 is all noun uses; examples were camera-only B1, no question

ex: The service here is very good.
Is service included in the bill?
Where is customer service, please?
This hotel has great service.
I play football on Saturdays.
We watch football on TV.
Football is my favorite sport.
Do you like football?

cash.say: pay in cash · Cash or card?
cash.why: no grammar line; add the key shop phrases

proof.say: proof of address · proof of age
proof.why: no grammar line; learners say 'a proof'

profit.say: make a profit · at a profit
profit.why: no grammar line; 'make a profit', not 'get a profit'

sense.say: make sense · no sense in · in a sense
sense.why: add 'make sense', the phrase used in the examples

internet.note: With "the": "on the internet". For a home connection, no "the": "Do you have internet?"
internet.why: note said always 'the', but two examples have no 'the'

mama.note: Childish or informal. Adults usually say "mom" (US) or "mum" (UK).
mama.why: add British 'mum', which Ukrainian schools teach

lunch.why: ланч is the usual menu word (бізнес-ланч), not slang

ID.why: айді is the normal reading of ID, like айті for IT
